scenario: D — Signals-only tenant (saas_premium, P1): accounts + communications, no KPI layer
narrative: They have CRM notes, tickets and Slack — and no usage data. The journey builds from evidence alone. docs/design/backlog-provisions.md P1, demo-narratives.md §7

communications.text: CRM contact update: Nadia Bell (VP Clinical Operations), the executive who sponsored the rollout, has left Halcyon for a role at a regional health system. Her deputy is covering but has not been named as owner.
With Nadia gone I'm going to pause our weekly check-ins until we've sorted out who owns the workflow programme internally. I'll be in touch when there's clarity.
QBR held as scheduled; nobody from Halcyon joined and Theo did not respond to the follow-up note.
Looking at the seat report you sent — roughly half of the licensed seats haven't logged in since the start of the year. The nursing teams that Nadia onboarded have mostly reverted to the old forms.
Ticket #3350: Fourth ticket this week from the discharge team — the approval routing keeps sending requests to a manager who no longer works here, and nobody on our side knows how to change the rule.
Only two people turned up to the admin training you ran; the rest of the invitees said they'd been told to hold off until the programme owner is decided.
Playbook 'exec sponsor rebuild' executed: our VP Customer met Owen Hart (COO) to re-establish sponsorship, and a value review with the interim clinical-systems team is booked for the 22nd.
Procurement is reviewing all software renewals above $500K this quarter and yours is on the list. Please send a usage summary and the current price per seat so we can benchmark it.
Following the review, we intend to renew at a reduced seat count — roughly 60% of the current licence. Theo will confirm the exact number, but please prepare a proposal on that basis.

events.title: Renewal at 60% of seats — Halcyon Health
events.evidence: Renewal order form dated 2026-04-30; seats reduced from 1,000 to 600

communications.text: We're rolling the workflow tool out to the regional merchandising team next month — about forty people. Can you send the onboarding checklist you used for store ops so we can reuse it?
The approvals module has really taken off — store managers are now building their own flows for stock transfers, which we never asked them to do.
Sofia asked what the analytics module would add on top of the standard reports and whether it could be trialled by the merchandising team before their rollout.
Heads up: API calls from our side have roughly tripled since the merchandising team started building flows against the inventory feed. Let us know if we're getting near any limits.
Daniel Cho (COO) joined the quarterly review for the first time and said the workflow programme is now one of his three operational priorities for the year.
We'd like a quote for an additional 150 seats to cover merchandising and the two new distribution centres, ideally co-termed with the current agreement.
Marketing is happy for us to do a case study on the store-ops rollout — send over the questions and we'll get it approved internally.
Ticket #3402: Page loads on the case queue have gone from two seconds to fifteen since last week's release; the operations floor is complaining and we've had to tell people to refresh.
The workaround you suggested means every case now needs an extra click to assign, and the team is grumbling that the tool has become harder to use than the spreadsheet it replaced.
Ticket #3419: Which export formats does the case queue support? We need CSV with UTF-8 headers for the monthly compliance extract.
The performance fix landed overnight and the case queue is back to normal — the floor has stopped complaining and the extra assignment click is gone. Thanks for turning that around.
FYI I left a five-star review on G2 this morning; the support turnaround on the performance issue was the main thing I called out.
Routine quarterly review with Femi: walked through the open requests and the roadmap; nothing flagged on either side.
Filled in the NPS survey — gave you a 9. The dispatch flows are doing exactly what we bought them for.
Routine monthly review with Femi: usage steady, one minor request about the mobile app logged, no concerns raised.
Sending over the meeting notes as promised — nothing new since we spoke.
Ticket #3511: The Guidewire sync is dropping about one claim in twenty and the claims team has stopped trusting the numbers in the workflow queue.
Escalating #3511 — it has been open for a week with no fix date, and we're now reconciling claims by hand every morning. I need an engineer on a call this week.
Until the Guidewire sync is fixed we've had to stop the rollout to the subrogation team — the integration is blocking the whole second phase.
Miguel has briefed me on the sync problem. I'd like a call with your leadership this week — this is now on my radar and I want a committed fix date before we discuss the second phase any further.
Ticket #3377: Feature request — could the approval step support a 'delegate for the week' setting? Our editors cover for each other during shoots.
Routine monthly review with Kai: covered the delegate request and the release notes; nothing else on the agenda.
